rows: Businesses must ensure hazardous waste causes no harm to people or the environment.
Waste should be classified to determine whether it is hazardous.
Hazardous waste should be separated and stored safely.
Only authorised carriers and permitted destination sites should be used.
Applicable hazardous-waste movements require consignment documentation.
Producers and holders should retain the required records.
Rejected loads and missing information require documented follow-up.
Hazardous waste transported by the producer remains subject to carrier requirements where applicable.
A consignment note or waste description does not prove lawful final management.
Conclusions require classification, quantity, storage, carrier, documentation, destination, permit and return evidence.
Business waste should be prevented, reused, recycled or recovered where reasonably practicable.
Waste must be sorted and stored safely and securely.
A waste transfer note is generally required for waste leaving business premises.
Businesses should check that waste carriers are registered.
Waste should be transferred only to authorised people and sites.
Businesses must not knowingly allow illegal disposal.
Records should support the description, quantity, carrier and destination of waste.
Suspected illegal waste activity should be reported through the appropriate route.
A carrier registration number does not prove that a specific waste movement is lawful.
Movement conclusions require waste identity, transfer note, carrier status, vehicle, destination, permit and receipt evidence.
Taking water from a surface or underground source is water abstraction.
An abstraction licence may be required depending on the activity and quantity.
Sources include rivers, streams, reservoirs, lakes, canals, tidal waters and groundwater.
Businesses should check licensing requirements before abstraction starts.
Exemptions and regulatory positions apply only when their conditions are met.
Groundwater investigations and dewatering can have separate requirements.
Operating without a required licence can lead to enforcement action.
Proposals should account for water availability and environmental effects.
A nearby water source or historic use does not prove that abstraction is exempt or licensed.
Conclusions require source, quantity, purpose, duration, location, exemption, licence and environmental evidence.
Licence holders must comply with the conditions on their abstraction or impounding licence.
Most licences require accurate measurement of abstracted water.
Records should show that abstraction remains within authorised quantities.
Returns must be submitted when the licence requires them.
A nil return may still be required when no water was abstracted.
Hands-off flow and drought restrictions must be followed.
Meters and measurement arrangements should be maintained and accurate.
Changes requiring more water should be authorised before exceeding licence limits.
A meter reading or licence copy does not prove full compliance.
Conclusions require licence conditions, measurements, returns, restrictions, meter accuracy, inspections and actual abstraction evidence.
